newsitem.title: UK: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, Feb 20.
newsitem.headline: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, Feb 20.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Thursday.

LONDON - London's FTSE 100 share index ended barely changed as a faltering Wall Street hauled it back from a new peak reached earlier in the session. The FTSE finished down 1.3 points at 4,356.1 after having clambered to an all-time high of 4,362.4 in morning trade.

FRANKFURT - German equities ended bourse trade down over one percentage point, marginally softer dollar and overnight declines on Wall Street stifle sentiment, but dealers say weakness sign of healthy correction with market at dizzy heights. The DAX-30 index ended at 3,196.03 down 37.72 points. In post-bourse trade the DAX index stood at 3,197.09.

PARIS - The French stockmarket finished lower as the bourse pursued a consolidation for a second day on its strong recent gains. "What everyone was expecting is happening -- an orderly consolidation. It's positive. It reminds people that the market doesn't only move in one direction," a trader said. The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished down 19.52 points or 0.75 percent at 2,575.24.

ZURICH - Swiss shares ended slightly higher and with a new record close after bouncing up and down during much of the session, trade was heavily influenced by derivatives-related transactions ahead of Friday's expiry of options and futures. The All-share Swiss Performance Index advanced 4.24 points or 0.15 percent to 2,875.19.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks surged, with the key market index closing above 19,000 for the first time in more than a month on a rally in property-related issues, property and bank shares gained ground on a newspaper report that the government may use public funds to buy land formerly owned by failed housing loan firms and other troubled financial firms. The Nikkei average of 225 leading issues rose 452.59 points or 2.43 percent to close at 19,051.71.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks blazed ahead to close with buoyant gains after the death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping allowed investors to put recent uncertainty behind them. The Hang Seng Index soared 305.01 points or 2.33 percent to close at 13,411.33.

SYDNEY - A combination of a battered bond market and profit-taking after its recent record breaking run pushed the Australian share market to a lower close, the death of Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping had no impact on the local market. The All Ordinaries index lost 14.70 points to 2,476.30.

JOHANNESBURG - South African industrial stocks perked up towards the close of the session, pushed up by what dealers said was firm two-way trade after drifting weaker for most of the day on a softer gold price, dealers said a slight weakening in the bullion price had also dulled the gold board, weighing down the All-share index which ended 5.1 points off its overnight record peak at 7,102.6, the Johannesburg Stock Exchange's Gold index shed 10.7 points to end at 1,470.9 while Industrials recouped earlier losses, rising 22.5 points to 8,391.7.
